38bec47fd4.q: What is Lens Factory's business model and how does it differ from traditional optometrists?
38bec47fd4.a: Lens Factory focuses on selling new lenses while customers keep their existing frames, rather than trying to sell complete new glasses. This is a niche service because when customers get a new prescription at traditional optometrists, those optometrists try to sell them entirely new frames. Lens Factory makes seven or eight thousand pairs of glasses a day and wants to help people see effectively by putting new lenses in frames they've already been styled for.

d483661959.q: What are the main types of optical lenses and how do progressive lenses differ from bifocals?
d483661959.a: Single vision lenses let you see at one distance—either close, intermediate like a computer, or far away. Bifocals have a small section at the bottom for close vision and the top for distance. Trifocals add a middle distance range. Progressive lenses are no-line bifocals or trifocals that give all three distance ranges depending on where you look in the lens, and digital progressive lenses provide an even larger field of vision compared to traditional bifocals where you have to move your head.

7bec22dbdb.q: What is Lens Factory's approach to customer service compared to AI chatbots?
7bec22dbdb.a: Lens Factory prioritizes having actual people answer calls and emails rather than relying on AI chatbots. While chatbots are useful for simple queries like order status, Lens Factory believes that for vision-related questions, customers need human support because people may not have the same understanding or knowledge about what they need. The company stresses that you can have great customer service with a mediocre product and customers will return, but a high-end product with horrible customer service won't bring customers back.
